title: Channels and backpressure
summary: Channel<T> as an in-process queue, why it must be bounded, the full modes, completion, and a producer/consumer pipeline that slows its producer down.

steps.title: Channel<T>: an async queue between producers and consumers
body: `System.Threading.Channels` (in the BCL since .NET Core 3.0) is the modern in-process queue: writers `await WriteAsync`, readers
`await foreach` over `ReadAllAsync`, and nobody blocks a thread.
```csharp fragment
var channel = Channel.CreateBounded<Order>(new BoundedChannelOptions(capacity: 100)
FullMode = BoundedChannelFullMode.Wait,   // a full channel makes WriteAsync wait: backpressure
SingleReader = false, SingleWriter = true
// producer                                   // consumer (one or many)
await channel.Writer.WriteAsync(order, ct);   await foreach (var o in channel.Reader.ReadAllAsync(ct))
channel.Writer.Complete();                         await HandleAsync(o, ct);
**Always bound it.** `Channel.CreateUnbounded` never pushes back: when consumers are slower than producers (a slow database, a
dependency down), the queue grows until the process runs out of memory. A bounded channel turns overload into *waiting*, which
travels back to whoever produces the work: that is **backpressure**.

steps.explain: `TryWrite` never waits: with the default `Wait` mode it returns false when full. Reading 1 makes room, so 3 fits now. A channel is FIFO.

steps.title: Completion and errors
body: - The producer calls `Writer.Complete()` when it has no more items. Readers drain what is left; `ReadAllAsync` then ends, and
`Reader.Completion` completes.
- `Writer.Complete(exception)` ends the channel with an error: `Reader.Completion` faults with it, so consumers can stop too.
- With **several consumers**, start them all, then `await Task.WhenAll(consumers)` after completing the writer: that is a clean
drain.
- `SingleReader = true` / `SingleWriter = true` are promises that let the channel use a faster implementation; break the promise and
you get corrupted state, not an exception.
Channels are the backbone of background work in ASP.NET Core: an endpoint writes a job, a `BackgroundService` reads and runs it
(module 7). A bounded channel there is how a burst of requests waits instead of filling memory.

steps.prompt: An endpoint enqueues e-mails into `Channel.CreateUnbounded<Email>()`, and a background service sends them. The mail provider is down for an hour. What happens?
options: The queue grows for the whole hour and the process may run out of memory; restarts lose everything queued
The channel drops old e-mails once it reaches its default capacity
WriteAsync waits until the provider is back
steps.explain: Unbounded means no limit and no pushback. Bound it, choose what happens when full (wait with a timeout, or reject with 503 / 429), and for work that must survive a restart use a durable queue (RabbitMQ, Kafka, a database outbox) instead of memory.

steps.prompt: Which full mode fits each case?
items: Order events: none may be lost; slow the producer instead
Live position updates for a map: only the latest few matter
Debug telemetry samples: losing new ones under load is fine
An import job reading a 10 GB file faster than it can write to the database

steps.title: A pipeline that pushes back
prompt: Write **`static async Task<int> RunPipelineAsync(IAsyncEnumerable<int> source, Func<int, Task> handle, int capacity, int consumers)`**:
- one producer reads `source` and writes every item into a **bounded** channel of `capacity` with `FullMode = Wait`;
- `consumers` consumer tasks read the channel and `await handle(item)` for each item;
- when the source ends, complete the writer, wait for all consumers to finish, and return how many items were handled.
The tests hold `handle` closed and count how far the producer read: with capacity 2 and one stuck consumer, it may read at most
**4** items (1 being handled, 2 in the channel, 1 waiting to be written).
starter: static async Task<int> RunPipelineAsync(IAsyncEnumerable<int> source, Func<int, Task> handle, int capacity, int consumers)
await foreach (var item in source) await channel.Writer.WriteAsync(item);

hints: Change `CreateUnbounded<int>()` to `CreateBounded<int>(new BoundedChannelOptions(capacity) { FullMode = BoundedChannelFullMode.Wait })` (with the full namespace).
The rest of the starter is right: start the consumers first, write everything, `Complete()`, then `await Task.WhenAll(workers)`.
explain: Start consumers *before* producing, or a bounded channel deadlocks itself: the producer waits for room that nobody makes. Counting
with `Interlocked` matters here: three consumers increment `handled` at the same time.
